title: מלחמת היהודים – כותרות הפרקים
title_en: The War of the Jews – chapter headings
note: כותרות הפרקים לפי תרגום ויליאם וויסטון (Sefaria); מספור: ספר:פרק.
note_de: Kapitelüberschriften aus William Whistons englischer Übersetzung (Sefaria), ins Deutsche übersetzt; Zählung Buch:Kapitel.
note_en: Chapter headings from William Whiston’s translation (Sefaria); numbering book:chapter.

items.text: How The City Jerusalem Was Taken, And The Temple Pillaged [By Antiochus Epiphanes]. As Also Concerning The Actions Of The Maccabees, Matthias And Judas; And Concerning The Death Of Judas.
items.text_de: Wie die Stadt Jerusalem eingenommen und der Tempel geplündert wurde [durch Antiochos Epiphanes]. Ferner über die Taten der Makkabäer Mattathias und Judas und über den Tod des Judas.
items.text_en: How The City Jerusalem Was Taken, And The Temple Pillaged [By Antiochus Epiphanes]. As Also Concerning The Actions Of The Maccabees, Matthias And Judas; And Concerning The Death Of Judas.

items.text: Concerning The Successors Of Judas, Who Were Jonathan And Simon, And John Hyrcanus.
items.text_de: Über die Nachfolger des Judas, nämlich Jonathan, Simon und Johannes Hyrkanos.
items.text_en: Concerning The Successors Of Judas, Who Were Jonathan And Simon, And John Hyrcanus.

items.text: How Aristobulus Was The First That Put A Diadem About His Head; And After He Had Put His Mother And Brother To Death, Died Himself, When He Had Reigned No More Than A Year.
items.text_de: Wie Aristobulos als Erster ein Diadem um sein Haupt legte und, nachdem er seine Mutter und seinen Bruder hatte töten lassen, selbst starb, als er nicht länger als ein Jahr regiert hatte.
items.text_en: How Aristobulus Was The First That Put A Diadem About His Head; And After He Had Put His Mother And Brother To Death, Died Himself, When He Had Reigned No More Than A Year.

items.text: What Actions Were Done By Alexander Janneus, Who Reigned Twenty-Seven Years.
items.text_de: Welche Taten Alexander Jannaios vollbrachte, der siebenundzwanzig Jahre regierte.
items.text_en: What Actions Were Done By Alexander Janneus, Who Reigned Twenty-Seven Years.

items.text: Alexandra Reigns Nine Years, During Which Time The Pharisees Were The Real Rulers Of The Nation.
items.text_de: Alexandra regiert neun Jahre, während derer die Pharisäer die eigentlichen Herrscher des Volkes waren.
items.text_en: Alexandra Reigns Nine Years, During Which Time The Pharisees Were The Real Rulers Of The Nation.

items.text: When Hyrcanus Who Was Alexander's Heir, Receded From His Claim To The Crown Aristobulus Is Made King; And Afterward The Same Hyrcanus By The Means Of Antipater, Is Brought Back By Abetas. At Last Pompey Is Made The Arbitrator Of The Dispute Between The Brothers.
items.text_de: Als Hyrkanos, der Erbe Alexanders, von seinem Anspruch auf die Krone zurücktritt, wird Aristobulos König; danach wird derselbe Hyrkanos mithilfe des Antipatros von Aretas zurückgeführt. Schließlich wird Pompeius zum Schiedsrichter im Streit zwischen den Brüdern bestimmt.
items.text_en: When Hyrcanus Who Was Alexander's Heir, Receded From His Claim To The Crown Aristobulus Is Made King; And Afterward The Same Hyrcanus By The Means Of Antipater, Is Brought Back By Abetas. At Last Pompey Is Made The Arbitrator Of The Dispute Between The Brothers.

items.text: How Pompey Had The City Of Jerusalem Delivered Up To Him But Took The Temple By Force. How He Went Into The Holy Of Holies; As Also What Were His Other Exploits In Judea.
items.text_de: Wie Pompeius sich die Stadt Jerusalem übergeben ließ, den Tempel aber mit Gewalt einnahm. Wie er in das Allerheiligste ging; ferner, welche weiteren Taten er in Judäa vollbrachte.
items.text_en: How Pompey Had The City Of Jerusalem Delivered Up To Him But Took The Temple By Force. How He Went Into The Holy Of Holies; As Also What Were His Other Exploits In Judea.

items.text: Alexander, The Son Of Aristobulus, Who Ran Away From Pompey, Makes An Expedition Against Hyrcanus; But Being Overcome By Gabinius He Delivers Up The Fortresses To Him. After This Aristobulus Escapes From Rome And Gathers An Army Together; But Being Beaten By The Romans, He Is Brought Back To Rome; With Other Things Relating To Gabinius, Crassus And Cassius.
items.text_de: Alexander, der Sohn des Aristobulos, der Pompeius entflohen war, zieht gegen Hyrkanos zu Felde; von Gabinius besiegt, übergibt er ihm die Festungen. Danach entkommt Aristobulos aus Rom und sammelt ein Heer; von den Römern geschlagen, wird er nach Rom zurückgebracht; nebst anderem, was Gabinius, Crassus und Cassius betrifft.
items.text_en: Alexander, The Son Of Aristobulus, Who Ran Away From Pompey, Makes An Expedition Against Hyrcanus; But Being Overcome By Gabinius He Delivers Up The Fortresses To Him. After This Aristobulus Escapes From Rome And Gathers An Army Together; But Being Beaten By The Romans, He Is Brought Back To Rome; With Other Things Relating To Gabinius, Crassus And Cassius.

items.text: Aristobulus Is Taken Off By Pompey's Friends, As Is His Son Alexander By Scipio. Antipater Cultivates A Friendship With Caesar, After Pompey's Death; He Also Performs Great Actions In That War, Wherein He Assisted Mithridates.
items.text_de: Aristobulos wird von den Freunden des Pompeius beseitigt, ebenso sein Sohn Alexander von Scipio. Antipatros pflegt nach dem Tod des Pompeius die Freundschaft Caesars; auch vollbringt er große Taten in jenem Krieg, in dem er Mithridates beistand.
items.text_en: Aristobulus Is Taken Off By Pompey's Friends, As Is His Son Alexander By Scipio. Antipater Cultivates A Friendship With Caesar, After Pompey's Death; He Also Performs Great Actions In That War, Wherein He Assisted Mithridates.

items.text: Caesar Makes Antipater Procurator Of Judea; As Does Antipater Appoint Phasaelus To Be Governor Of Jerusalem, And Herod Governor Of Galilee; Who, In Some Time, Was Called To Answer For Himself [Before The Sanhedrim], Where He Is Acquitted. Sextus Caesar Is Treacherously Killed By Bassus And Is Succeeded By Marcus.
items.text_de: Caesar macht Antipatros zum Prokurator von Judäa; Antipatros wiederum setzt Phasael zum Statthalter von Jerusalem und Herodes zum Statthalter von Galiläa ein; dieser wird nach einiger Zeit zur Verantwortung gezogen [vor dem Synedrion] und dort freigesprochen. Sextus Caesar wird von Bassus heimtückisch ermordet, und Marcus folgt ihm nach.
items.text_en: Caesar Makes Antipater Procurator Of Judea; As Does Antipater Appoint Phasaelus To Be Governor Of Jerusalem, And Herod Governor Of Galilee; Who, In Some Time, Was Called To Answer For Himself [Before The Sanhedrim], Where He Is Acquitted. Sextus Caesar Is Treacherously Killed By Bassus And Is Succeeded By Marcus.

items.text: Herod Is Made Procurator Of All Syria; Malichus Is Afraid Of Him, And Takes Antipater Off By Poison; Whereupon The Tribunes Of The Soldiers Are Prevailed With To Kill Him.
items.text_de: Herodes wird zum Prokurator von ganz Syrien gemacht; Malichos fürchtet ihn und beseitigt Antipatros durch Gift; daraufhin werden die Kriegstribunen bewogen, ihn zu töten.
items.text_en: Herod Is Made Procurator Of All Syria; Malichus Is Afraid Of Him, And Takes Antipater Off By Poison; Whereupon The Tribunes Of The Soldiers Are Prevailed With To Kill Him.

items.text: Phasaelus Is Too Hard For Felix; Herod Also Overcomes Antigonus In Rattle; And The Jews Accuse Both Herod And Phasaelus But Antonius Acquits Them, And Makes Them Tetrarchs.
items.text_de: Phasael ist Felix überlegen; auch Herodes besiegt Antigonos in der Schlacht; die Juden klagen sowohl Herodes als auch Phasael an, doch Antonius spricht sie frei und macht sie zu Tetrarchen.
items.text_en: Phasaelus Is Too Hard For Felix; Herod Also Overcomes Antigonus In Rattle; And The Jews Accuse Both Herod And Phasaelus But Antonius Acquits Them, And Makes Them Tetrarchs.

items.text: The Parthians Bring Antigonus Back Into Judea, And Cast Hyrcanus And Phasaelus Into Prison. The Flight Of Herod, And The Taking Of Jerusalem And What Hyrcanus And Phasaelus Suffered.
items.text_de: Die Parther führen Antigonos nach Judäa zurück und werfen Hyrkanos und Phasael ins Gefängnis. Die Flucht des Herodes, die Einnahme Jerusalems und was Hyrkanos und Phasael erlitten.
items.text_en: The Parthians Bring Antigonus Back Into Judea, And Cast Hyrcanus And Phasaelus Into Prison. The Flight Of Herod, And The Taking Of Jerusalem And What Hyrcanus And Phasaelus Suffered.

items.text: When Herod Is Rejected In Arabia, He Makes Haste To Rome Where Antony And Caesar Join Their Interest To Make Him King .
items.text_de: Als Herodes in Arabien abgewiesen wird, eilt er nach Rom, wo Antonius und Caesar ihren Einfluss vereinen, um ihn zum König zu machen.
items.text_en: When Herod Is Rejected In Arabia, He Makes Haste To Rome Where Antony And Caesar Join Their Interest To Make Him King .

items.text: Antigonus Besieges Those That Were In Masada, Whom Herod Frees From Confinement When He Came Back From Rome, And Presently Marches To Jerusalem Where He Finds Silo Corrupted By Bribes.
items.text_de: Antigonos belagert die in Masada Eingeschlossenen, die Herodes bei seiner Rückkehr aus Rom aus ihrer Bedrängnis befreit; bald darauf zieht er nach Jerusalem, wo er Silo durch Bestechung verdorben findet.
items.text_en: Antigonus Besieges Those That Were In Masada, Whom Herod Frees From Confinement When He Came Back From Rome, And Presently Marches To Jerusalem Where He Finds Silo Corrupted By Bribes.

items.text: Herod Takes Sepphoris And Subdues The Robbers That Were In The Caves ; He After That Avenges Himself Upon Macheras, As Upon An Enemy Of His And Goes To Antony As He Was Besieging Samosata.
items.text_de: Herodes nimmt Sepphoris ein und bezwingt die Räuber, die sich in den Höhlen befanden; danach rächt er sich an Machairas als an seinem Feind und begibt sich zu Antonius, der gerade Samosata belagerte.
items.text_en: Herod Takes Sepphoris And Subdues The Robbers That Were In The Caves ; He After That Avenges Himself Upon Macheras, As Upon An Enemy Of His And Goes To Antony As He Was Besieging Samosata.

items.text: The Death Of Joseph [Herod's Brother] Which Had Been Signified To Herod In Dreams. How Herod Was Preserved Twice After A Wonderful Manner. He Cuts Off The Head Of Pappus, Who Was The Murderer Of His Brother And Sends That Head To [His Other Brother] Pheroras, And In No Long Time He Besieges Jerusalem And Marries Mariamne.
items.text_de: Der Tod Josephs [des Bruders des Herodes], der Herodes in Träumen angekündigt worden war. Wie Herodes zweimal auf wunderbare Weise gerettet wurde. Er schlägt Pappos, dem Mörder seines Bruders, den Kopf ab und schickt diesen Kopf [seinem anderen Bruder] Pheroras; bald darauf belagert er Jerusalem und heiratet Mariamne.
items.text_en: The Death Of Joseph [Herod's Brother] Which Had Been Signified To Herod In Dreams. How Herod Was Preserved Twice After A Wonderful Manner. He Cuts Off The Head Of Pappus, Who Was The Murderer Of His Brother And Sends That Head To [His Other Brother] Pheroras, And In No Long Time He Besieges Jerusalem And Marries Mariamne.

items.text: How Herod And Sosius Took Jerusalem By Force; And What Death Antigonus Came To. Also Concerning Cleopatra's Avaricious Temper.
items.text_de: Wie Herodes und Sosius Jerusalem mit Gewalt einnahmen und welches Ende Antigonos fand. Ferner über die Habgier Kleopatras.
items.text_en: How Herod And Sosius Took Jerusalem By Force; And What Death Antigonus Came To. Also Concerning Cleopatra's Avaricious Temper.

items.text: How Antony At The Persuasion Of Cleopatra Sent Herod To Fight Against The Arabians; And Now After Several Battles, He At Length Got The Victory. As Also Concerning A Great Earthquake.
items.text_de: Wie Antonius auf Drängen Kleopatras Herodes gegen die Araber in den Kampf schickte und wie dieser nach mehreren Schlachten schließlich den Sieg errang. Ferner über ein großes Erdbeben.
items.text_en: How Antony At The Persuasion Of Cleopatra Sent Herod To Fight Against The Arabians; And Now After Several Battles, He At Length Got The Victory. As Also Concerning A Great Earthquake.

items.text: Herod Is Confirmed In His Kingdom By Caesar, And Cultivates A Friendship With The Emperor By Magnificent Presents; While Caesar Returns His Kindness By Bestowing On Him That Part Of His Kingdom Which Had Been Taken Away From It By Cleopatra With The Addition Of Zenodoruss Country Also.
items.text_de: Herodes wird von Caesar in seinem Königtum bestätigt und pflegt die Freundschaft des Kaisers durch prächtige Geschenke; Caesar erwidert seine Freundlichkeit, indem er ihm den Teil seines Königreichs zurückgibt, den Kleopatra davon abgetrennt hatte, und ihm dazu auch noch das Land des Zenodoros verleiht.
items.text_en: Herod Is Confirmed In His Kingdom By Caesar, And Cultivates A Friendship With The Emperor By Magnificent Presents; While Caesar Returns His Kindness By Bestowing On Him That Part Of His Kingdom Which Had Been Taken Away From It By Cleopatra With The Addition Of Zenodoruss Country Also.

items.text: Of The [Temple And] Cities That Were Built By Herod And Erected From The Very Foundations; As Also Of Those Other Edifices That Were Erected By Him; And What Magnificence He Showed To Foreigners; And How Fortune Was In All Things Favorable To Him.
items.text_de: Über den [Tempel und die] Städte, die Herodes von Grund auf erbaute und errichtete; ferner über die anderen Bauwerke, die er errichtete; welche Großzügigkeit er gegenüber Fremden zeigte und wie ihm das Glück in allen Dingen hold war.
items.text_en: Of The [Temple And] Cities That Were Built By Herod And Erected From The Very Foundations; As Also Of Those Other Edifices That Were Erected By Him; And What Magnificence He Showed To Foreigners; And How Fortune Was In All Things Favorable To Him.

items.text: The Murder Of Aristobulus And Hyrcanus, The High Priests, As Also Of Mariamne The Queen.
items.text_de: Die Ermordung der Hohepriester Aristobulos und Hyrkanos sowie der Königin Mariamne.
items.text_en: The Murder Of Aristobulus And Hyrcanus, The High Priests, As Also Of Mariamne The Queen.

items.text: Calumnies Against The Sons Of Mariamne. Antipateris Preferred Before Them. They Are Accused Before Caesar, And Herod Is Reconciled To Them.
items.text_de: Verleumdungen gegen die Söhne Mariamnes. Antipatros wird ihnen vorgezogen. Sie werden vor Caesar angeklagt, und Herodes versöhnt sich mit ihnen.
items.text_en: Calumnies Against The Sons Of Mariamne. Antipateris Preferred Before Them. They Are Accused Before Caesar, And Herod Is Reconciled To Them.

items.text: The Malice Of Antipater And Doris. Alexander Is Very Uneasy On Glaphyras Account. Herod Pardons Pheroras, Whom He Suspected, And Salome Whom He Knew To Make Mischief Among Them. Herod's Eunuchs Are Tortured And Alexander Is Bound.
items.text_de: Die Bosheit des Antipatros und der Doris. Alexander ist wegen Glaphyra sehr beunruhigt. Herodes verzeiht Pheroras, den er im Verdacht hatte, und Salome, von der er wusste, dass sie Unfrieden unter ihnen stiftete. Die Eunuchen des Herodes werden gefoltert, und Alexander wird in Fesseln gelegt.
items.text_en: The Malice Of Antipater And Doris. Alexander Is Very Uneasy On Glaphyras Account. Herod Pardons Pheroras, Whom He Suspected, And Salome Whom He Knew To Make Mischief Among Them. Herod's Eunuchs Are Tortured And Alexander Is Bound.

items.text: Archelaus Procures A Reconciliation Between Alexander Pheroras, And Herod.
items.text_de: Archelaos bewirkt eine Versöhnung zwischen Alexander, Pheroras und Herodes.
items.text_en: Archelaus Procures A Reconciliation Between Alexander Pheroras, And Herod.

items.text: How Eurycles Calumniated The Sons Of Mariamne; And How Euaratus Of Cos Apology For Them Had No Effect.
items.text_de: Wie Eurykles die Söhne Mariamnes verleumdete und wie die Verteidigung des Euaratos von Kos für sie ohne Wirkung blieb.
items.text_en: How Eurycles Calumniated The Sons Of Mariamne; And How Euaratus Of Cos Apology For Them Had No Effect.

items.text: Herod By Caesars Direction Accuses His Sons At Eurytus. They Are Not Produced Before The Courts But Yet Are Condemned; And In A Little Time They Are Sent To Sebaste, And Strangled There.
items.text_de: Herodes klagt auf Anweisung Caesars seine Söhne in Berytos an. Sie werden nicht vor Gericht vorgeführt und dennoch verurteilt; kurz darauf werden sie nach Sebaste gebracht und dort erdrosselt.
items.text_en: Herod By Caesars Direction Accuses His Sons At Eurytus. They Are Not Produced Before The Courts But Yet Are Condemned; And In A Little Time They Are Sent To Sebaste, And Strangled There.

items.text: How Antipater Is Hated Of All Men; And How The King Espouses The Sons Of Those That Had Been Slain To His Kindred;But That Antipater Made Him Change Them For Other Women. Of Herod's Marriages, And Children.
items.text_de: Wie Antipatros von allen Menschen gehasst wird; wie der König die Kinder der Getöteten mit seinen Verwandten verlobt, Antipatros ihn aber dazu bringt, sie mit anderen Frauen zu tauschen. Über die Ehen und Kinder des Herodes.
items.text_en: How Antipater Is Hated Of All Men; And How The King Espouses The Sons Of Those That Had Been Slain To His Kindred;But That Antipater Made Him Change Them For Other Women. Of Herod's Marriages, And Children.

items.text: Antipater Becomes Intolerable. He Is Sent To Rome, And Carries Herod's Testament With Him; Pheroras Leaves His Brother, That He May Keep His Wife. He Dies At Home.
items.text_de: Antipatros wird unerträglich. Er wird nach Rom geschickt und nimmt das Testament des Herodes mit; Pheroras verlässt seinen Bruder, um seine Frau behalten zu können. Er stirbt zu Hause.
items.text_en: Antipater Becomes Intolerable. He Is Sent To Rome, And Carries Herod's Testament With Him; Pheroras Leaves His Brother, That He May Keep His Wife. He Dies At Home.

items.text: When Herod Made Inquiry About Pheroras's Death A Discovery Was Made That Antipater Had Prepared A Poisonous Draught For Him. Herod Casts Doris And Her Accomplices, As Also Mariamne, Out Of The Palace And Blots Her Son Herod Out Of His Testament.
items.text_de: Als Herodes Nachforschungen über den Tod des Pheroras anstellte, wurde entdeckt, dass Antipatros einen Gifttrank für ihn bereitet hatte. Herodes verstößt Doris und ihre Mitwisser sowie Mariamne aus dem Palast und streicht ihren Sohn Herodes aus seinem Testament.
items.text_en: When Herod Made Inquiry About Pheroras's Death A Discovery Was Made That Antipater Had Prepared A Poisonous Draught For Him. Herod Casts Doris And Her Accomplices, As Also Mariamne, Out Of The Palace And Blots Her Son Herod Out Of His Testament.

items.text: Antipater Is Convicted By Bathyllus ; But He Still Returns From Rome Without Knowing It. Herod Brings Him To His Trial.
items.text_de: Antipatros wird durch Bathyllos überführt; er kehrt dennoch aus Rom zurück, ohne davon zu wissen. Herodes stellt ihn vor Gericht.
items.text_en: Antipater Is Convicted By Bathyllus ; But He Still Returns From Rome Without Knowing It. Herod Brings Him To His Trial.

items.text: Antipater Is Accused Before Varus, And Is Convicted Of Laying A Plot [Against His Father] By The Strongest Evidence. Herod Puts Off His Punishment Till He Should Be Recovered, And In The Mean Time Alters His Testament.
items.text_de: Antipatros wird vor Varus angeklagt und durch die stärksten Beweise überführt, einen Anschlag [gegen seinen Vater] geplant zu haben. Herodes verschiebt seine Bestrafung, bis er selbst genesen sei, und ändert in der Zwischenzeit sein Testament.
items.text_en: Antipater Is Accused Before Varus, And Is Convicted Of Laying A Plot [Against His Father] By The Strongest Evidence. Herod Puts Off His Punishment Till He Should Be Recovered, And In The Mean Time Alters His Testament.

items.text: The Golden Eagle Is Cut To Pieces. Herod's Barbarity When He Was Ready To Die. He Attempts To Kill Himself. He Commands Antipater To Be Slain. He Survives Him Five Days And Then Dies.
items.text_de: Der goldene Adler wird in Stücke geschlagen. Die Grausamkeit des Herodes, als er dem Tode nahe war. Er versucht, sich selbst zu töten. Er befiehlt, Antipatros hinzurichten. Er überlebt ihn um fünf Tage und stirbt dann.
items.text_en: The Golden Eagle Is Cut To Pieces. Herod's Barbarity When He Was Ready To Die. He Attempts To Kill Himself. He Commands Antipater To Be Slain. He Survives Him Five Days And Then Dies.

items.text: Archelaus Makes A Funeral Feast For The People, On The Account Of Herod. After Which A Great Tumult Is Raised By The Multitude And He Sends The Soldiers Out Upon Them, Who Destroy About Three Thousand Of Them.
items.text_de: Archelaos richtet für das Volk um des Herodes willen ein Leichenmahl aus. Danach erhebt die Menge einen großen Aufruhr, und er schickt die Soldaten gegen sie aus, die etwa dreitausend von ihnen töten.
items.text_en: Archelaus Makes A Funeral Feast For The People, On The Account Of Herod. After Which A Great Tumult Is Raised By The Multitude And He Sends The Soldiers Out Upon Them, Who Destroy About Three Thousand Of Them.

items.text: Archelaus Goes To Rome With A Great Number Of His Kindred. He Is There Accused Before Caesar By Antipater; But Is Superior To His Accusers In Judgment By The Means Of That Defense Which Nicolaus Made For Him.
items.text_de: Archelaos reist mit einer großen Zahl seiner Verwandten nach Rom. Dort wird er von Antipatros vor Caesar angeklagt, behält aber vor Gericht die Oberhand über seine Ankläger dank der Verteidigung, die Nikolaos für ihn führte.
items.text_en: Archelaus Goes To Rome With A Great Number Of His Kindred. He Is There Accused Before Caesar By Antipater; But Is Superior To His Accusers In Judgment By The Means Of That Defense Which Nicolaus Made For Him.

items.text: The Jews Fight A Great Battle With Sabinus's Soldiers, And A Great Destruction Is Made At Jerusalem.
items.text_de: Die Juden liefern den Soldaten des Sabinus eine große Schlacht, und in Jerusalem wird ein großes Blutbad angerichtet.
items.text_en: The Jews Fight A Great Battle With Sabinus's Soldiers, And A Great Destruction Is Made At Jerusalem.

items.text: Herod's Veteran Soldiers Become Tumultuous. The Robberies Of Judas. Simon And Athronoeus Take The Name Of King Upon Them.
items.text_de: Die Veteranen des Herodes werden aufrührerisch. Die Räubereien des Judas. Simon und Athronges legen sich den Königstitel bei.
items.text_en: Herod's Veteran Soldiers Become Tumultuous. The Robberies Of Judas. Simon And Athronoeus Take The Name Of King Upon Them.

items.text: Varus Composes The Tumults In Judea And Crucifies About Two Thousand Of The Seditious.
items.text_de: Varus schlichtet die Unruhen in Judäa und lässt etwa zweitausend der Aufrührer kreuzigen.
items.text_en: Varus Composes The Tumults In Judea And Crucifies About Two Thousand Of The Seditious.

items.text: The Jews Greatly Complain Of Archelaus And Desire That They May Be Made Subject To Roman Governors. But When Caesar Had Heard What They Had To Say, He Distributed Herod's Dominions Among His Sons According To His Own Pleasure.
items.text_de: Die Juden beklagen sich heftig über Archelaos und begehren, römischen Statthaltern unterstellt zu werden. Nachdem Caesar aber angehört hatte, was sie zu sagen hatten, verteilte er die Herrschaftsgebiete des Herodes nach eigenem Gutdünken unter dessen Söhne.
items.text_en: The Jews Greatly Complain Of Archelaus And Desire That They May Be Made Subject To Roman Governors. But When Caesar Had Heard What They Had To Say, He Distributed Herod's Dominions Among His Sons According To His Own Pleasure.

items.text: The History Of The Spurious Alexander. Archelaus Is Banished And Glaphyra Dies, After What Was To Happen To Both Of Them Had Been Showed Them In Dreams.
items.text_de: Die Geschichte des falschen Alexander. Archelaos wird verbannt, und Glaphyra stirbt, nachdem beiden in Träumen gezeigt worden war, was ihnen widerfahren sollte.
items.text_en: The History Of The Spurious Alexander. Archelaus Is Banished And Glaphyra Dies, After What Was To Happen To Both Of Them Had Been Showed Them In Dreams.

items.text: Archelaus's Ethnarchy Is Reduced Into A [Roman] Province. The Sedition Of Judas Of Galilee. The Three Sects.
items.text_de: Das Ethnarchat des Archelaos wird in eine [römische] Provinz umgewandelt. Der Aufruhr des Judas von Galiläa. Die drei Sekten.
items.text_en: Archelaus's Ethnarchy Is Reduced Into A [Roman] Province. The Sedition Of Judas Of Galilee. The Three Sects.

items.text: The Death Of Salome. The Cities Which Herod And Philip Built. Pilate Occasions Disturbances. Tiberius Puts Agrippa Into Bonds But Caius Frees Him From Them, And Makes Him King. Herod Antipas Is Banished.
items.text_de: Der Tod Salomes. Die Städte, die Herodes und Philippus erbauten. Pilatus verursacht Unruhen. Tiberius legt Agrippa in Fesseln, Gaius aber befreit ihn daraus und macht ihn zum König. Herodes Antipas wird verbannt.
items.text_en: The Death Of Salome. The Cities Which Herod And Philip Built. Pilate Occasions Disturbances. Tiberius Puts Agrippa Into Bonds But Caius Frees Him From Them, And Makes Him King. Herod Antipas Is Banished.

items.text: Caius Commands That His Statue Should Be Set Up In The Temple Itself; And What Petronius Did Thereupon.
items.text_de: Gaius befiehlt, seine Statue im Tempel selbst aufzustellen; und was Petronius daraufhin tat.
items.text_en: Caius Commands That His Statue Should Be Set Up In The Temple Itself; And What Petronius Did Thereupon.

items.text: Concerning The Government Of Claudius, And The Reign Of Agrippa. Concerning The Deaths Of Agrippa And Of Herod And What Children They Both Left Behind Them.
items.text_de: Über die Regierung des Claudius und die Herrschaft Agrippas. Über den Tod Agrippas und des Herodes und welche Kinder beide hinterließen.
items.text_en: Concerning The Government Of Claudius, And The Reign Of Agrippa. Concerning The Deaths Of Agrippa And Of Herod And What Children They Both Left Behind Them.

items.text: Many Tumults Under Cumanus, Which Were Composed By Quadratus. Felix Is Procurator Of Judea. Agrippa Is Advanced From Chalcis To A Greater Kingdom.
items.text_de: Viele Unruhen unter Cumanus, die von Quadratus geschlichtet wurden. Felix ist Prokurator von Judäa. Agrippa wird von Chalkis zu einem größeren Königreich befördert.
items.text_en: Many Tumults Under Cumanus, Which Were Composed By Quadratus. Felix Is Procurator Of Judea. Agrippa Is Advanced From Chalcis To A Greater Kingdom.

items.text: Nero Adds Four Cities To Agrippas Kingdom; But The Other Parts Of Judea Were Under Felix. The Disturbances Which Were Raised By The Sicarii The Magicians And An Egyptian False Prophet. The Jews And Syrians Have A Contest At Cesarea.
items.text_de: Nero fügt dem Königreich Agrippas vier Städte hinzu; die übrigen Teile Judäas aber standen unter Felix. Die Unruhen, die von den Sikariern, den Zauberern und einem ägyptischen falschen Propheten ausgelöst wurden. Juden und Syrer geraten in Caesarea in Streit.
items.text_en: Nero Adds Four Cities To Agrippas Kingdom; But The Other Parts Of Judea Were Under Felix. The Disturbances Which Were Raised By The Sicarii The Magicians And An Egyptian False Prophet. The Jews And Syrians Have A Contest At Cesarea.

items.text: Festus Succeeds Felix Who Is Succeeded By Albinus As He Is By Florus; Who By The Barbarity Of His Government Forces The Jews Into The War.
items.text_de: Festus folgt Felix nach, ihm folgt Albinus und diesem Florus, der die Juden durch die Grausamkeit seiner Herrschaft in den Krieg treibt.
items.text_en: Festus Succeeds Felix Who Is Succeeded By Albinus As He Is By Florus; Who By The Barbarity Of His Government Forces The Jews Into The War.

items.text: Concerning Bernice's Petition To Florus, To Spare The Jews, But In Vain; As Also How, After The Seditious Flame Was Quenched, It Was Kindled Again By Florus.
items.text_de: Über Berenikes Bitte an Florus, die Juden zu schonen, die jedoch vergeblich war; ferner, wie die Flamme des Aufruhrs, nachdem sie gelöscht worden war, von Florus erneut entfacht wurde.
items.text_en: Concerning Bernice's Petition To Florus, To Spare The Jews, But In Vain; As Also How, After The Seditious Flame Was Quenched, It Was Kindled Again By Florus.

items.text: Cestius Sends Neopolitanus The Tribune To See In What Condition The Affairs Of The Jews Were. Agrippa Makes A Speech To The People Of The Jews That He May Divert Them From Their Intentions Of Making War With The Romans.
items.text_de: Cestius sendet den Tribun Neopolitanus, um zu erkunden, in welchem Zustand sich die Angelegenheiten der Juden befänden. Agrippa hält eine Rede an das Volk der Juden, um sie von ihrer Absicht abzubringen, Krieg gegen die Römer zu führen.
items.text_en: Cestius Sends Neopolitanus The Tribune To See In What Condition The Affairs Of The Jews Were. Agrippa Makes A Speech To The People Of The Jews That He May Divert Them From Their Intentions Of Making War With The Romans.

items.text: How The War Of The Jews With The Romans Began, And Concerning Manahem.
items.text_de: Wie der Krieg der Juden gegen die Römer begann; und über Menahem.
items.text_en: How The War Of The Jews With The Romans Began, And Concerning Manahem.

items.text: The Calamities And Slaughters That Came Upon The Jews.
items.text_de: Die Unglücksfälle und Gemetzel, die über die Juden kamen.
items.text_en: The Calamities And Slaughters That Came Upon The Jews.

items.text: What Cestius Did Against The Jews; And How, Upon His Besieging Jerusalem, He Retreated From The City Without Any Just Occasion In The World. As Also What Severe Calamities He Under Went From The Jews In His Retreat.
items.text_de: Was Cestius gegen die Juden unternahm und wie er bei der Belagerung Jerusalems ohne jeden triftigen Grund von der Stadt abzog. Ferner, welche schweren Verluste er auf seinem Rückzug durch die Juden erlitt.
items.text_en: What Cestius Did Against The Jews; And How, Upon His Besieging Jerusalem, He Retreated From The City Without Any Just Occasion In The World. As Also What Severe Calamities He Under Went From The Jews In His Retreat.

items.text: Cestius Sends Ambassadors To Nero. The People Of Damascus Slay Those Jews That Lived With Them. The People Of Jerusalem After They Had [Left Off] Pursuing Cestius, Return To The City And Get Things Ready For Its Defense And Make A Great Many Generals For, Their Armies And Particularly Josephus The Writer Of These Books. Some Account Of His Administration.
items.text_de: Cestius sendet Gesandte zu Nero. Die Einwohner von Damaskus töten die Juden, die unter ihnen lebten. Nachdem die Bewohner Jerusalems [davon abgelassen hatten,] Cestius zu verfolgen, kehren sie in die Stadt zurück, bereiten ihre Verteidigung vor und ernennen sehr viele Feldherren für ihre Heere, insbesondere Josephus, den Verfasser dieser Bücher. Ein Bericht über seine Amtsführung.
items.text_en: Cestius Sends Ambassadors To Nero. The People Of Damascus Slay Those Jews That Lived With Them. The People Of Jerusalem After They Had [Left Off] Pursuing Cestius, Return To The City And Get Things Ready For Its Defense And Make A Great Many Generals For, Their Armies And Particularly Josephus The Writer Of These Books. Some Account Of His Administration.

items.text: Concerning John Of Gischala. Josephus Uses Stratagems Against The Plots John Laid Against Him And Recovers Certain Cities Which Had Revolted From Him.
items.text_de: Über Johannes von Gischala. Josephus begegnet den Anschlägen, die Johannes gegen ihn plante, mit Kriegslisten und gewinnt gewisse Städte zurück, die von ihm abgefallen waren.
items.text_en: Concerning John Of Gischala. Josephus Uses Stratagems Against The Plots John Laid Against Him And Recovers Certain Cities Which Had Revolted From Him.

items.text: The Jews Make All Ready For The War; And Simon, The Son Of Gioras, Falls To Plundering.
items.text_de: Die Juden rüsten sich vollständig für den Krieg; und Simon bar Giora verlegt sich aufs Plündern.
items.text_en: The Jews Make All Ready For The War; And Simon, The Son Of Gioras, Falls To Plundering.

items.text: Vespasian Is Sent Into Syria By Nero In Order To Make War With The Jews.
items.text_de: Vespasian wird von Nero nach Syrien gesandt, um Krieg gegen die Juden zu führen.
items.text_en: Vespasian Is Sent Into Syria By Nero In Order To Make War With The Jews.

items.text: A Great Slaughter About Ascalon. Vespasian Comes To Ptolemais.
items.text_de: Ein großes Gemetzel bei Askalon. Vespasian kommt nach Ptolemaïs.
items.text_en: A Great Slaughter About Ascalon. Vespasian Comes To Ptolemais.

items.text: A Description Op Galilee, Samaria, And Judea.
items.text_de: Eine Beschreibung von Galiläa, Samaria und Judäa.
items.text_en: A Description Op Galilee, Samaria, And Judea.

items.text: Josephus Makes An Attempt Upon Sepphoris But Is Repelled. Titus Comes With A Great Army To Ptolemais.
items.text_de: Josephus unternimmt einen Angriff auf Sepphoris, wird aber zurückgeschlagen. Titus kommt mit einem großen Heer nach Ptolemaïs.
items.text_en: Josephus Makes An Attempt Upon Sepphoris But Is Repelled. Titus Comes With A Great Army To Ptolemais.

items.text: A Description Of The Roman Armies And Roman Camps And Of Other Particulars For Which The Romans Are Commended.
items.text_de: Eine Beschreibung der römischen Heere und römischen Lager und anderer Einzelheiten, für die die Römer gerühmt werden.
items.text_en: A Description Of The Roman Armies And Roman Camps And Of Other Particulars For Which The Romans Are Commended.

items.text: Placidus Attempts To Take Jotapata And Is Beaten Off. Vespasian Marches Into Galilee.
items.text_de: Placidus versucht, Jotapata einzunehmen, und wird zurückgeschlagen. Vespasian zieht nach Galiläa.
items.text_en: Placidus Attempts To Take Jotapata And Is Beaten Off. Vespasian Marches Into Galilee.

items.text: Vespasian, When He Had Taken The City Gadara Marches To Jotapata. After A Long Siege The City Is Betrayed By A Deserter, And Taken By Vespasian.
items.text_de: Nachdem Vespasian die Stadt Gadara eingenommen hat, zieht er nach Jotapata. Nach langer Belagerung wird die Stadt von einem Überläufer verraten und von Vespasian eingenommen.
items.text_en: Vespasian, When He Had Taken The City Gadara Marches To Jotapata. After A Long Siege The City Is Betrayed By A Deserter, And Taken By Vespasian.

items.text: How Josephus Was Discovered By A Woman, And Was Willing To Deliver Himself Up To The Romans; And What Discourse He Had With His Own Men, When They Endeavored To Hinder Him; And What He Said To Vespasian, When He Was Brought To Him; And After What Manner Vespasian Used Him Afterward.
items.text_de: Wie Josephus von einer Frau verraten wurde und bereit war, sich den Römern zu ergeben; welches Gespräch er mit seinen eigenen Leuten führte, als sie ihn daran zu hindern suchten; was er zu Vespasian sagte, als er zu ihm gebracht wurde; und wie Vespasian ihn danach behandelte.
items.text_en: How Josephus Was Discovered By A Woman, And Was Willing To Deliver Himself Up To The Romans; And What Discourse He Had With His Own Men, When They Endeavored To Hinder Him; And What He Said To Vespasian, When He Was Brought To Him; And After What Manner Vespasian Used Him Afterward.

items.text: How Joppa Was Taken, And Tiberias Delivered Up.
items.text_de: Wie Joppe eingenommen und Tiberias übergeben wurde.
items.text_en: How Joppa Was Taken, And Tiberias Delivered Up.

items.text: How Taricheae Was Taken. A Description Of The River Jordan, And Of The Country Of Gennesareth.
items.text_de: Wie Tarichea eingenommen wurde. Eine Beschreibung des Flusses Jordan und der Landschaft Gennesaret.
items.text_en: How Taricheae Was Taken. A Description Of The River Jordan, And Of The Country Of Gennesareth.

items.text: The Siege And Taking Of Gamala.
items.text_de: Die Belagerung und Einnahme von Gamala.
items.text_en: The Siege And Taking Of Gamala.

items.text: The Surrender Of Gischala; While John Flies Away From It To Jerusalem.
items.text_de: Die Übergabe von Gischala, während Johannes von dort nach Jerusalem flieht.
items.text_en: The Surrender Of Gischala; While John Flies Away From It To Jerusalem.

items.text: Concerning John Of Gischala. Concerning The Zealots And The High Priest Ananus; As Also How The Jews Raise Seditions One Against Another [In Jerusalem].
items.text_de: Über Johannes von Gischala. Über die Zeloten und den Hohepriester Ananos; ferner, wie die Juden [in Jerusalem] Aufruhr gegeneinander erheben.
items.text_en: Concerning John Of Gischala. Concerning The Zealots And The High Priest Ananus; As Also How The Jews Raise Seditions One Against Another [In Jerusalem].

items.text: The Idumeans Being Sent For By The Zealots, Came Immediately To Jerusalem; And When They Were Excluded Out Of The City, They Lay All Night There. Jesus One Of The High Priests Makes A Speech To Them; And Simon The Idumean Makes A Reply To It.
items.text_de: Die Idumäer, von den Zeloten herbeigerufen, kamen sogleich nach Jerusalem; und als man sie aus der Stadt ausschloss, lagerten sie die ganze Nacht dort. Jesus, einer der Hohepriester, hält eine Rede an sie, und Simon der Idumäer antwortet darauf.
items.text_en: The Idumeans Being Sent For By The Zealots, Came Immediately To Jerusalem; And When They Were Excluded Out Of The City, They Lay All Night There. Jesus One Of The High Priests Makes A Speech To Them; And Simon The Idumean Makes A Reply To It.

items.text: The Cruelty Of The Idumeans When They Were Gotten Into The Temple During The Storm; And Of The Zealots. Concerning The Slaughter Of Ananus, And Jesus, And Zacharias; And How The Idumeans Retired Home.
items.text_de: Die Grausamkeit der Idumäer, als sie während des Unwetters in den Tempel gelangt waren, und die der Zeloten. Über die Ermordung des Ananos, des Jesus und des Zacharias; und wie die Idumäer nach Hause zurückkehrten.
items.text_en: The Cruelty Of The Idumeans When They Were Gotten Into The Temple During The Storm; And Of The Zealots. Concerning The Slaughter Of Ananus, And Jesus, And Zacharias; And How The Idumeans Retired Home.

items.text: How The Zealots When They Were Freed From The Idumeans, Slew A Great Many More Of The Citizens; And How Vespasian Dissuaded The Romans When They Were Very Earnest To March Against The Jews From Proceeding In The War At That Time.
items.text_de: Wie die Zeloten, nachdem sie von den Idumäern befreit waren, noch sehr viele weitere Bürger töteten; und wie Vespasian die Römer, die eifrig darauf drängten, gegen die Juden zu ziehen, davon abbrachte, den Krieg zu jener Zeit fortzusetzen.
items.text_en: How The Zealots When They Were Freed From The Idumeans, Slew A Great Many More Of The Citizens; And How Vespasian Dissuaded The Romans When They Were Very Earnest To March Against The Jews From Proceeding In The War At That Time.

items.text: How John Tyrannized Over The Rest; And What Mischiefs The Zealots Did At Masada. How Also Vespasian Took Gadara; And What Actions Were Performed By Placidus.
items.text_de: Wie Johannes über die Übrigen eine Gewaltherrschaft ausübte und welches Unheil die Zeloten in Masada anrichteten. Ferner, wie Vespasian Gadara einnahm und welche Taten Placidus vollbrachte.
items.text_en: How John Tyrannized Over The Rest; And What Mischiefs The Zealots Did At Masada. How Also Vespasian Took Gadara; And What Actions Were Performed By Placidus.

items.text: Made Haste To Finish The Jewish War. A Description Of. Jericho, And Of The Great Plain; With An Account Besides Of The Lake Asphaltitis.
items.text_de: … beeilte sich, den Jüdischen Krieg zu beenden. Eine Beschreibung von Jericho und der großen Ebene, nebst einem Bericht über den Asphaltsee.
items.text_en: Made Haste To Finish The Jewish War. A Description Of. Jericho, And Of The Great Plain; With An Account Besides Of The Lake Asphaltitis.

items.text: That Vespasian, After He Had Taken Gadara Made Preparation For The Siege Of Jerusalem; But That, Upon His Hearing Of The Death Of Nero, He Changed His Intentions. As Also Concerning Simon Of Geras.
items.text_de: Dass Vespasian, nachdem er Gadara eingenommen hatte, Vorbereitungen zur Belagerung Jerusalems traf, seine Absichten aber änderte, als er vom Tod Neros hörte. Ferner über Simon aus Gerasa.
items.text_en: That Vespasian, After He Had Taken Gadara Made Preparation For The Siege Of Jerusalem; But That, Upon His Hearing Of The Death Of Nero, He Changed His Intentions. As Also Concerning Simon Of Geras.

items.text: How The Soldiers, Both In Judea And Egypt, Proclaimed Vespasian Emperor;And How Vespasian Released Josephus From His Bonds.
items.text_de: Wie die Soldaten in Judäa und in Ägypten Vespasian zum Kaiser ausriefen und wie Vespasian Josephus von seinen Fesseln befreite.
items.text_en: How The Soldiers, Both In Judea And Egypt, Proclaimed Vespasian Emperor;And How Vespasian Released Josephus From His Bonds.

items.text: That Upon The Conquest And Slaughter Of Vitellius Vespasian Hastened His Journey To Rome; But Titus His Son Returned To Jerusalem.
items.text_de: Dass Vespasian nach dem Sieg über Vitellius und dessen Tötung seine Reise nach Rom beschleunigte, sein Sohn Titus aber nach Jerusalem zurückkehrte.
items.text_en: That Upon The Conquest And Slaughter Of Vitellius Vespasian Hastened His Journey To Rome; But Titus His Son Returned To Jerusalem.

items.text: Concerning The Seditions At Jerusalem And What Terrible Miseries Afflicted The City By Their Means.
items.text_de: Über die Aufstände in Jerusalem und welch schreckliches Elend dadurch über die Stadt kam.
items.text_en: Concerning The Seditions At Jerusalem And What Terrible Miseries Afflicted The City By Their Means.

items.text: How Titus Marched To Jerusalem, And How He Was In Danger As He Was Taking A View O The City Of The Place Also Where He Pitched His Camp
items.text_de: Wie Titus nach Jerusalem zog und wie er in Gefahr geriet, als er die Stadt erkundete; ferner über den Ort, an dem er sein Lager aufschlug.
items.text_en: How Titus Marched To Jerusalem, And How He Was In Danger As He Was Taking A View O The City Of The Place Also Where He Pitched His Camp

items.text: How The Sedition Was Again Revived Within Jerusalem And Yet The Jews Contrived Snares For The Romans. How Titus Also Threatened His Soldiers For Their Ungovernable Rashness.
items.text_de: Wie der Aufruhr in Jerusalem von Neuem auflebte und die Juden dennoch den Römern Fallen stellten. Ferner, wie Titus seinen Soldaten wegen ihres zügellosen Ungestüms drohte.
items.text_en: How The Sedition Was Again Revived Within Jerusalem And Yet The Jews Contrived Snares For The Romans. How Titus Also Threatened His Soldiers For Their Ungovernable Rashness.

items.text: The Description Of Jerusalem.
items.text_de: Die Beschreibung Jerusalems.
items.text_en: The Description Of Jerusalem.

items.text: A Description Of The Temple.
items.text_de: Eine Beschreibung des Tempels.
items.text_en: A Description Of The Temple.

items.text: Concerning The Tyrants Simon And John. How Also As Titus Was Going Round The Wall Of This City Nicanor Was Wounded By A Dart; Which Accident Provoked Titus To Press On The Siege.
items.text_de: Über die Tyrannen Simon und Johannes. Ferner, wie Nikanor, als Titus um die Mauer dieser Stadt herumging, von einem Wurfspieß verwundet wurde; dieser Vorfall veranlasste Titus, die Belagerung voranzutreiben.
items.text_en: Concerning The Tyrants Simon And John. How Also As Titus Was Going Round The Wall Of This City Nicanor Was Wounded By A Dart; Which Accident Provoked Titus To Press On The Siege.

items.text: How One Of The Towers Erected By The Romans Fell Down Of Its Own Accord; And How The Romans After Great Slaughter Had Been Made Got Possession Of The First Wall. How Also Titus Made His Assaults Upon The Second Wall; As Also Concerning Longinus The Roman, And Castor The Jew.
items.text_de: Wie einer der von den Römern errichteten Türme von selbst einstürzte und wie die Römer nach einem großen Gemetzel die erste Mauer in Besitz nahmen. Ferner, wie Titus seine Angriffe auf die zweite Mauer richtete; ferner über den Römer Longinus und den Juden Kastor.
items.text_en: How One Of The Towers Erected By The Romans Fell Down Of Its Own Accord; And How The Romans After Great Slaughter Had Been Made Got Possession Of The First Wall. How Also Titus Made His Assaults Upon The Second Wall; As Also Concerning Longinus The Roman, And Castor The Jew.

items.text: How The Romans Took The Second Wall Twice, And Got All Ready For Taking The Third Wall.
items.text_de: Wie die Römer die zweite Mauer zweimal einnahmen und alles für die Einnahme der dritten Mauer vorbereiteten.
items.text_en: How The Romans Took The Second Wall Twice, And Got All Ready For Taking The Third Wall.

items.text: Titus When The Jews Were Not At All Mollified By His Leaving Off The Siege For A While, Set Himself Again To Prosecute The Same; But Soon Sent Josephus To Discourse With His Own Countrymen About Peace.
items.text_de: Als die Juden dadurch, dass Titus die Belagerung eine Zeit lang aussetzte, keineswegs besänftigt wurden, machte er sich erneut daran, sie fortzusetzen; bald aber sandte er Josephus, um mit seinen eigenen Landsleuten über Frieden zu reden.
items.text_en: Titus When The Jews Were Not At All Mollified By His Leaving Off The Siege For A While, Set Himself Again To Prosecute The Same; But Soon Sent Josephus To Discourse With His Own Countrymen About Peace.

items.text: How A Great Many Of The People Earnestly Endeavored To Desert To The Romans; As Also What Intolerable Things Those That Staid Behind Suffered By Famine, And The Sad Consequences Thereof.
items.text_de: Wie sehr viele aus dem Volk eifrig versuchten, zu den Römern überzulaufen; ferner, welch unerträgliche Leiden die Zurückgebliebenen durch die Hungersnot erduldeten, und deren traurige Folgen.
items.text_en: How A Great Many Of The People Earnestly Endeavored To Desert To The Romans; As Also What Intolerable Things Those That Staid Behind Suffered By Famine, And The Sad Consequences Thereof.

items.text: How The Jews Were Crucified Before The Walls Of The City Concerning Antiochus Epiphanes; And How The Jews Overthrew The Banks That Had Been Raised By The Romans,
items.text_de: Wie die Juden vor den Mauern der Stadt gekreuzigt wurden. Über Antiochos Epiphanes; und wie die Juden die von den Römern aufgeworfenen Wälle zerstörten.
items.text_en: How The Jews Were Crucified Before The Walls Of The City Concerning Antiochus Epiphanes; And How The Jews Overthrew The Banks That Had Been Raised By The Romans,

items.text: Titus Thought Fit To Encompass The City Round With A Wall; After Which The Famine Consumed The People By Whole Houses And Families Together.
items.text_de: Titus hielt es für angebracht, die Stadt ringsum mit einer Mauer einzuschließen; danach raffte die Hungersnot das Volk in ganzen Häusern und Familien dahin.
items.text_en: Titus Thought Fit To Encompass The City Round With A Wall; After Which The Famine Consumed The People By Whole Houses And Families Together.

items.text: The Great Slaughters And Sacrilege That Were In Jerusalem.
items.text_de: Die großen Gemetzel und Tempelschändungen, die in Jerusalem geschahen.
items.text_en: The Great Slaughters And Sacrilege That Were In Jerusalem.

items.text: That the Miseries Still Grew Worse; and how the Romans Made an Assault upon the Tower of Antonia.
items.text_de: Dass das Elend immer schlimmer wurde; und wie die Römer einen Angriff auf die Burg Antonia unternahmen.
items.text_en: That the Miseries Still Grew Worse; and how the Romans Made an Assault upon the Tower of Antonia.

items.text: How Titus Gave Orders To Demolish The Tower Of Antonia And Then Persuaded Josephus To Exhort The Jews Again [To A Surrender].
items.text_de: Wie Titus befahl, die Burg Antonia zu schleifen, und dann Josephus bewog, die Juden erneut [zur Übergabe] zu ermahnen.
items.text_en: How Titus Gave Orders To Demolish The Tower Of Antonia And Then Persuaded Josephus To Exhort The Jews Again [To A Surrender].

items.text: Concerning A Stratagem That Was Devised By The Jews, By Which They Burnt Many Of The Romans; With Another Description Of The Terrible Famine That Was In The City.
items.text_de: Über eine von den Juden ersonnene Kriegslist, durch die sie viele Römer verbrannten; nebst einer weiteren Beschreibung der schrecklichen Hungersnot, die in der Stadt herrschte.
items.text_en: Concerning A Stratagem That Was Devised By The Jews, By Which They Burnt Many Of The Romans; With Another Description Of The Terrible Famine That Was In The City.

items.text: When The Banks Were Completed And The Battering Rams Brought, And Could Do Nothing, Titus Gave Orders To Set Fire To The Gates Of The Temple; In No Long Time After Which The Holy House Itself Was Burnt Down, Even Against His Consent.
items.text_de: Als die Wälle fertiggestellt und die Sturmböcke herangebracht waren, aber nichts ausrichten konnten, befahl Titus, die Tore des Tempels in Brand zu setzen; nicht lange danach brannte das heilige Haus selbst nieder, und zwar gegen seinen Willen.
items.text_en: When The Banks Were Completed And The Battering Rams Brought, And Could Do Nothing, Titus Gave Orders To Set Fire To The Gates Of The Temple; In No Long Time After Which The Holy House Itself Was Burnt Down, Even Against His Consent.

items.text: The Great Distress The Jews Were In Upon The Conflagration Of The Holy House. Concerning A False Prophet, And The Signs That Preceded This Destruction.
items.text_de: Die große Not, in der sich die Juden beim Brand des heiligen Hauses befanden. Über einen falschen Propheten und die Zeichen, die dieser Zerstörung vorausgingen.
items.text_en: The Great Distress The Jews Were In Upon The Conflagration Of The Holy House. Concerning A False Prophet, And The Signs That Preceded This Destruction.

items.text: How The Romans Carried Their Ensigns To The Temple, And Made Joyful Acclamations To Titus. The Speech That Titus Made To The Jews When They Made Supplication For Mercy. What Reply They Made Thereto; And How That Reply Moved Titus's Indignation Against Them.
items.text_de: Wie die Römer ihre Feldzeichen zum Tempel trugen und Titus mit Jubel zuriefen. Die Rede, die Titus an die Juden hielt, als sie um Gnade flehten. Was sie darauf antworteten und wie diese Antwort den Zorn des Titus gegen sie erregte.
items.text_en: How The Romans Carried Their Ensigns To The Temple, And Made Joyful Acclamations To Titus. The Speech That Titus Made To The Jews When They Made Supplication For Mercy. What Reply They Made Thereto; And How That Reply Moved Titus's Indignation Against Them.

items.text: What Afterward Befell The Seditious When They Had Done A Great Deal Of Mischief, And Suffered Many Misfortunes; As Also How Caesar Became Master Of The Upper City,
items.text_de: Was den Aufrührern danach widerfuhr, nachdem sie viel Unheil angerichtet und viele Unglücksfälle erlitten hatten; ferner, wie Caesar Herr der Oberstadt wurde.
items.text_en: What Afterward Befell The Seditious When They Had Done A Great Deal Of Mischief, And Suffered Many Misfortunes; As Also How Caesar Became Master Of The Upper City,

items.text: How Caesar Raised Banks Round About The Upper City [Mount Zion] And When They Were Completed, Gave Orders That The Machines Should Be Brought. He Then Possessed Himself Of The Whole City.
items.text_de: Wie Caesar rings um die Oberstadt [den Berg Zion] Wälle aufwerfen ließ und nach deren Fertigstellung befahl, die Belagerungsmaschinen heranzubringen. Daraufhin bemächtigte er sich der ganzen Stadt.
items.text_en: How Caesar Raised Banks Round About The Upper City [Mount Zion] And When They Were Completed, Gave Orders That The Machines Should Be Brought. He Then Possessed Himself Of The Whole City.

items.text: What Injunctions Caesar Gave When He Was Come Within The City. The Number Of The Captives And Of Those That Perished In The Siege; As Also Concerning Those That Had Escaped Into The Subterranean Caverns, Among Whom Were The Tyrants Simon And John Themselves.
items.text_de: Welche Anordnungen Caesar gab, als er in die Stadt gelangt war. Die Zahl der Gefangenen und derer, die bei der Belagerung umkamen; ferner über diejenigen, die in die unterirdischen Höhlen geflohen waren, darunter die Tyrannen Simon und Johannes selbst.
items.text_en: What Injunctions Caesar Gave When He Was Come Within The City. The Number Of The Captives And Of Those That Perished In The Siege; As Also Concerning Those That Had Escaped Into The Subterranean Caverns, Among Whom Were The Tyrants Simon And John Themselves.

items.text: That Whereas The City Of Jerusalem Had Been Five Times Taken Formerly, This Was The Second Time Of Its Desolation. A Brief Account Of Its History.
items.text_de: Dass, während die Stadt Jerusalem früher schon fünfmal eingenommen worden war, dies das zweite Mal ihrer Verwüstung war. Ein kurzer Abriss ihrer Geschichte.
items.text_en: That Whereas The City Of Jerusalem Had Been Five Times Taken Formerly, This Was The Second Time Of Its Desolation. A Brief Account Of Its History.

items.text: How The Entire City Of Jerusalem Was Demolished, Excepting Three Towers; And How Titus Commended His Soldiers In A Speech Made To Them, And Distributed Rewards To Them And Then Dismissed Many Of Them.
items.text_de: Wie die ganze Stadt Jerusalem bis auf drei Türme geschleift wurde; und wie Titus seine Soldaten in einer an sie gerichteten Rede lobte, ihnen Belohnungen austeilte und dann viele von ihnen entließ.
items.text_en: How The Entire City Of Jerusalem Was Demolished, Excepting Three Towers; And How Titus Commended His Soldiers In A Speech Made To Them, And Distributed Rewards To Them And Then Dismissed Many Of Them.

items.text: How Titus Exhibited All Sorts Of Shows At Cesarea Philippi. Concerning Simon The Tyrant How He Was Taken, And Reserved For The Triumph.
items.text_de: Wie Titus in Caesarea Philippi allerlei Schauspiele veranstaltete. Über den Tyrannen Simon, wie er gefangen genommen und für den Triumph aufbewahrt wurde.
items.text_en: How Titus Exhibited All Sorts Of Shows At Cesarea Philippi. Concerning Simon The Tyrant How He Was Taken, And Reserved For The Triumph.

items.text: How Titus Upon The Celebration Of His Brothers And Fathers Birthdays Had Many Of The Jews Slain. Concerning The Danger The Jews Were In At Antioch, By Means Of The Transgression And Impiety Of One Antiochus, A Jew.
items.text_de: Wie Titus bei der Feier der Geburtstage seines Bruders und seines Vaters viele Juden töten ließ. Über die Gefahr, in der sich die Juden in Antiochia befanden, durch die Missetat und Gottlosigkeit eines gewissen Antiochos, eines Juden.
items.text_en: How Titus Upon The Celebration Of His Brothers And Fathers Birthdays Had Many Of The Jews Slain. Concerning The Danger The Jews Were In At Antioch, By Means Of The Transgression And Impiety Of One Antiochus, A Jew.

items.text: How Vespasian Was Received At Rome; As Also How The Germans Revolted From The Romans, But Were Subdued. That The Sarmatians Overran Mysia, But Were Compelled To Retire To Their Own Country Again.
items.text_de: Wie Vespasian in Rom empfangen wurde; ferner, wie die Germanen von den Römern abfielen, aber unterworfen wurden. Dass die Sarmaten Mysien überrannten, aber gezwungen wurden, sich wieder in ihr eigenes Land zurückzuziehen.
items.text_en: How Vespasian Was Received At Rome; As Also How The Germans Revolted From The Romans, But Were Subdued. That The Sarmatians Overran Mysia, But Were Compelled To Retire To Their Own Country Again.

items.text: Concerning The Sabbatic River Which Titus Saw As He Was Journeying Through Syria; And How The People Of Antioch Came With A Petition To Titus Against The Jews But Were Rejected By Him; As Also Concerning Titus's And Vespasian's Triumph.
items.text_de: Über den Sabbatfluss, den Titus auf seiner Reise durch Syrien sah; und wie die Einwohner von Antiochia mit einer Bittschrift gegen die Juden zu Titus kamen, aber von ihm abgewiesen wurden; ferner über den Triumph des Titus und Vespasians.
items.text_en: Concerning The Sabbatic River Which Titus Saw As He Was Journeying Through Syria; And How The People Of Antioch Came With A Petition To Titus Against The Jews But Were Rejected By Him; As Also Concerning Titus's And Vespasian's Triumph.

items.text: Concerning Macherus, And How Lucilius Bassus Took That Citadel, And Other Places.
items.text_de: Über Machärus und wie Lucilius Bassus diese Festung und andere Orte einnahm.
items.text_en: Concerning Macherus, And How Lucilius Bassus Took That Citadel, And Other Places.

items.text: Concerning The Calamity That Befell Antiochus, King Of Commagene. As Also Concerning The Alans And What Great Mischiefs They Did To The Medes And Armenians.
items.text_de: Über das Unglück, das Antiochos, den König von Kommagene, traf. Ferner über die Alanen und welch großes Unheil sie den Medern und Armeniern zufügten.
items.text_en: Concerning The Calamity That Befell Antiochus, King Of Commagene. As Also Concerning The Alans And What Great Mischiefs They Did To The Medes And Armenians.

items.text: Concerning Masada And Those Sicarii Who Kept It; And How Silva Betook Himself To Form The Siege Of That Citadel. Eleazar's Speeches To The Besieged.
items.text_de: Über Masada und die Sikarier, die es besetzt hielten; und wie Silva sich daranmachte, diese Festung zu belagern. Die Reden Eleazars an die Belagerten.
items.text_en: Concerning Masada And Those Sicarii Who Kept It; And How Silva Betook Himself To Form The Siege Of That Citadel. Eleazar's Speeches To The Besieged.

items.text: How The People That Were In The Fortress Were Prevailed On By The Words Of Eleazar, Two Women And Five Children Only Excepted And All Submitted To Be Killed By One Another.
items.text_de: Wie die Leute in der Festung durch die Worte Eleazars überredet wurden – nur zwei Frauen und fünf Kinder ausgenommen – und sich alle dazu hergaben, einander zu töten.
items.text_en: How The People That Were In The Fortress Were Prevailed On By The Words Of Eleazar, Two Women And Five Children Only Excepted And All Submitted To Be Killed By One Another.

items.text: That Many Of The Sicarii Fled To Alexandria Also And What Dangers They Were In There; On Which Account That Temple Which Had Formerly Been Built By Onias The High Priest Was Destroyed.
items.text_de: Dass viele der Sikarier auch nach Alexandria flohen und in welche Gefahren sie dort gerieten; weswegen der Tempel, den einst der Hohepriester Onias erbaut hatte, zerstört wurde.
items.text_en: That Many Of The Sicarii Fled To Alexandria Also And What Dangers They Were In There; On Which Account That Temple Which Had Formerly Been Built By Onias The High Priest Was Destroyed.

items.text: Concerning Jonathan, One Of The Sicarii, That Stirred Up A Sedition In Cyrene, And Was A False Accuser [Of The Innocent].
items.text_de: Über Jonathan, einen der Sikarier, der in Kyrene einen Aufruhr anzettelte und ein falscher Ankläger [der Unschuldigen] war.
items.text_en: Concerning Jonathan, One Of The Sicarii, That Stirred Up A Sedition In Cyrene, And Was A False Accuser [Of The Innocent].
